title: promote-latest.mjs: ensureGitHubRelease makes one attempt, so an upstream HTTP 500 still leaves the Release uncut
description: Follow-up from the LCLI-689 review (NOTE 11). After LCLI-689 a lagging read no longer skips the GitHub Release step, but ensureGitHubRelease still makes a single attempt: an upstream GitHub HTTP 500 (as on 0.13.0, 2026-10-07) leaves the Release uncut at exit 3, needing an out-of-band repair. Consider a bounded retry. Not built in LCLI-689.
implementationNotes: Non-blocking nit from the Opus review of opum-ai/lore-cli#645 (opum-doc): ensureGitHubRelease forwards lagOptions.sleep and delayMs (the npm-verify test seam, verifyOptions) into the release retry, so the two waits share a seam. Give the release retry its own option. Not done in #645; file as a follow-up task if wanted.
finalSummary: ensureGitHubRelease now retries a bounded RELEASE_ATTEMPTS=3, 5s apart, only on isTransientReleaseFailure; every attempt starts with ensureGitHubReleaseOnce read, so a create that reached GitHub is found and finished rather than made twice. Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#645 (CI run 39813648687 attempt 2 green on 5dc115fb after one rerun of the ubuntu epoll race). Opus review by opum-doc: APPROVE. The retry never republishes to a registry.
